title: KV island reintegration and prefill handoff simulator
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem statement: In heavy multi-tenant serving with paged attention, small *islands* of KV memory (sparsely used fragments) are created by long-tail session patterns. These islands increase fragmentation, reduce effective residency for hot contexts, and cause repeated prefill/eviction churn when kernel selection and prefill points are misaligned. Current heuristics treat page eviction and prefill admission independently which causes oscillation and higher tail latency for decodes.

Goals:
- Model and simulate 'island reintegration' strategies that proactively merge small KV islands into adjacent pages or temporarily co-locate decode kernels to reduce fetch overlap.
- Design a prefill handoff policy where a prefill operation that discovers a thin island can either (A) reintegrate by copying minimal deltas into a target page, (B) register a lightweight alias to avoid extra kernel fetches, or (C) schedule a cooperative decode on the same GPU to amortize fetch cost.
- Evaluate how kernel selection (fast low-precision vs. robust high-precision kernels), attention window tuning, and prefill scheduling interact with reintegration choices.
- Produce an offline simulator + microbenchmarks that predict token tail latency and effective residency under different workload mixes (short chat vs. long-context summarization).

Design approach:
1) Simulation model: build an agent-based simulator that represents pages, fragments, tenants, and kernels. The simulator will accept workload traces (sampling from production prefix length distributions) and emulate: allocation, fragment accession, aliasing, copy-on-reintegrate, eviction, and kernel selection decisions. Simulator outputs: per-tenant tail latencies (p95/p99/p999), page occupancy heatmap, effective reuse ratio, and prefill-induced network/GPU fetch volume.

2) Reintegration primitives (prototype API):
- alias_register(page_id, fragment_id): low-cost pointer to avoid copying if future accesses are localized.
- delta_merge(src_fragment, dst_page): copy only the non-overlapping token vectors and update mapping.
- cooperative_decode_schedule(fragment_id, kernel_hint): schedule next decode for same GPU within prefill horizon to exploit warm caches.

3) Kernel-aware policy: map reintegration decisions to kernel selection signals. E.g., if kernel_hint==fast_f32q and fragment occupancy is low, prefer aliasing; if robust_kernel required and fragment expected reuse > threshold, prefer delta_merge.

Acceptance criteria:
- Simulator can replay a 24-hour production trace in under 30 minutes on a devbox and produce stable metrics.
- Microbenchmarks show at least 20% reduction in prefill fetch volume or 10% improvement in p99 decode latency for the short-long mixed workload compared to baseline heuristics.
- Patch with reintegration primitives and a toggled policy flag behind runtime feature gate that can be A/B tested on a limited Dedicated pool.

Testing and rollout:
- Unit tests for mapping logic and correctness of aliasing/merge semantics.
- End-to-end microbench against a synthetic blend (80% 32-token chat, 20% 8k-token summarization) in a local Dedicated cluster.
- Canary on a single Dedicated tenant with feature gate + telemetry (prefill fetch bytes, p99 decode latency, page churn rate).

Risks and mitigations:
- Copying fragments introduces extra writeback pressure: mitigate by delta-copy thresholds and background low-priority merges.
- Alias complexity can increase lookup latency: ensure alias resolution is O(1) and inline in the KV mapping layer; add metrics to track alias indirections.
- Mis-prediction for kernel choice may regress accuracy/latency tradeoffs: add conservative defaults and rollback signal when p999 latency increases.

Open questions:
- What is the expected cost budget for background delta merges before it affects tail SLOs?
- How to encode reuse prediction signal cheaply (per-fragment touch counters vs. ML model)?
- Should reintegration be tenant-scoped to avoid cross-tenant co-location for sensitive workloads?

2025-02-24 - Design review notes: PM asked we preserve tenant isolation; decision: reintegration may co-locate only within tenant scope by default. Cross-tenant policies require explicit opt-in.

2025-02-27 - Marco Li: Ran 24h trace run; simulator completes in 18 minutes on m5.large dev VM. Preliminary metric: delta_merge + cooperative_decode reduces p99 by ~12% for mixed workloads, meets target. Filing PR for runtime shim (WIP).
